title: Qualitative Evaluation of YouTube Videos on Dental Fear, Anxiety and Phobia
screen_reason: Content analysis of the 100 most-viewed YouTube videos for each of three search terms (dental fear, dental anxiety, dental phobia), 145 eligible after screening. Two coders independently judged whether each video contained misleading information and report 17 videos (11.7%) that did, with Cohen's kappa 93%. The paper lists the specific errors coded (e.g. 'Dental fear and dental phobia are the same thing', 'Laughing gas is not sedation'), so these are truth judgements against the clinical literature, not a completeness or usability score. Denominator of items that exist in the sampled set, so CONTENT.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language YouTube search run by a Hong Kong team
estimates.date: Search conducted 25 October 2022 (videos uploaded March 2007 - September 2022)
estimates.measure_type: % of dental fear/anxiety/phobia YouTube videos containing misleading information
estimates.denominator: 145 English-language YouTube videos on dental fear, dental anxiety or dental phobia included after screening the 100 most-viewed results for each of three search terms (300 screened, 181 after duplicate removal)
estimates.definition: Two independent coders judged the video content to contain misleading information, i.e. statements contradicting the clinical/psychological literature (examples given: equating dental fear with dental phobia; claiming 'specific dental phobia' is an established term; claiming dental phobia is a DSM diagnosis; claiming laughing gas is not sedation; grouping all psychological and non-pharmacological treatments together; a title claiming new drugs for dental anxiety)
estimates.misinfo_def: The paper gives no formal definition; misleading content is enumerated as specific 'Misinformation: ... Truth: ...' pairs in the Discussion, e.g. "Misinformation: Dental fear and dental phobia are the same thing. Truth: They differ in"
estimates.source_quote: and 17 videos (11.7%) contained misleading information. The Cohen’s kappa of whether the included videos contained misleading information was 93%.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two investigators watched every video independently and coded content thematically: a psychology PhD student (NW) and a dentist experienced in evaluating dental YouTube videos (AY). Disagreements resolved by discussion. Cohen's kappa for the misleading-information judgement = 93%; kappa for eligibility screening = 94.7%.
estimates.moderator_quote: The terms dental fear, dental anxiety, and dental phobia were searched on the YouTube home page. The first 100 most widely viewed videos that resulted from each search term were recorded and screened. Hence, a total of 300 videos were correspondingly screened for eligibility.
estimates.notes: denom_selection=curated because the frame is the top 100 most-viewed results per term, a rank-truncated set. country_norm=Global: no country restriction is stated for the videos, only English language.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted as separate rows: the view-count breakdown in Table 11 (high-view group 19.4% with misleading information vs low-view group 4.1%, p = 0.004, median split at 5756 views), and the non-significant breakdowns by video source (lay public 23.8%, professions 9.0%, others 12.5%, p = 0.158) and by informant (health professions 12.5%, non-health 10.2%, p = 0.684). These are subgroup splits of the same 145-video denominator rather than distinct measures; the instructions say to keep the main figure. The high-view result is flagged in the abstract, so it could be argued as a headline subgroup, but 11.7% is the paper's prevalence number. Also not extracted: 51.0% (n = 74) of videos contained commercial information and 24.8% (n = 36) gave a dental clinic contact - commercial disclosure, not veracity. The abstract's finding that videos lacked definitional or diagnostic information is a coverage gap, not a falsity share.

rob.design: Cross-sectional qualitative content analysis of YouTube, searched 25 October 2022; screening completed within 14 days to limit platform churn. Frame: first 100 most-viewed videos per search term for 'dental fear', 'dental anxiety' and 'dental phobia' (1626 videos identified, 300 screened, 181 after duplicate removal, 145 included). Exclusions: irrelevant content (cartoon, game, role-play, pure entertainment, music/meditation) and non-English videos. Two independent investigators (a psychology PhD student and a dentist) screened and coded every video; disagreements resolved by discussion. Reliability: Cohen's kappa 94.7% for eligibility, 93% for the misleading-information judgement. Chi-squared tests for group differences, SPSS 26.0, alpha .05. No formal a priori codebook for 'misleading' is presented; the criterion is the coders' expert judgement, with examples given post hoc in the Discussion.
rob.item6_quote: Chi-squared tests were conducted to evaluate if the proportion of videos with misinformation was significantly different between video groups, in terms of the video source (lay public, professions versus others), informant identity (health professions versus non-health professions), and view count (high view versus low view, binarized by median split).
rob.item10_quote: A total of 145 videos were included in the final analysis. ... and 17 videos (11.7%) contained misleading information.
